newsitem.title: UK: Japan drug sales recovery is temporary - IMS.
newsitem.headline: Japan drug sales recovery is temporary - IMS.

text.p: A sharp recovery in drug sales in Japan in March is likely to be only temporary, with the outlook for the rest of 1997 poor, research group IMS International said on Monday.

In the first three months of 1997 sales of drugs rose by six percent in local currency terms, totalling $9.98 billion, IMS said. This compared with a gain of just one percent in local currency terms in January and February.

IMS said the gains were driven by growth in cardiovascular and alimentary drugs, as well as cyclical factors, including a severe flu epidemic, a related increase in coughs and colds and a rise in cedar tree pollen allergies.
These factors were reflected in a ten percent rise in sales of anti-infective products, while respiratory sales jumped 26 percent and sensory organ drugs rose 24 percent.
"However the turnaround is expected to be only temporary and the outlook for the rest of the year is poor," IMS said.
It said sales in April were likely to be affected by government price revisions, and added that the approval process for new products had slowed.

In a recently published study on the international pharmaceutical market, IMS said Japanese drug sales were likely to rise by three percent a year between 1997 and 2001, the lowest rate of any developed market.

"The pharmaceutical industry in Japan will face tough operating conditions in the years to come with prospects for individual Japanese companies largely dependent on their product pipelines," IMS said.
